questions.a: Those who serve Yahweh in his temple and courtyards should praise Yahweh.

questions.q: Why should those who serve Yahweh praise and sing to him?
questions.a: They should praise Yahweh because he is good, and they should sing praises to him because doing that is pleasant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh chose the descendants of Jacob, the people of Israel, to belong only to him as his special possession.

questions.q: What does the psalmist know about Yahweh?
questions.a: He knows that Yahweh is great, he is more powerful than all other gods, and he does whatever he wants to do anywhere on earth or in heaven.

questions.q: What acts does Yahweh do that show his greatness?
questions.a: Yahweh brings the clouds, makes lightning bolts accompany the rain, and brings the wind from wherever he stores it.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do to the Egyptians?
questions.a: He killed the firstborn man and animals of Egypt and he did amazing miracles against Pharaoh and all his servants.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do with the land of the nations that other kings ruled over?
questions.a: He gave their land as an inheritance to Israel his people.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s name, and what does Yahweh do for his people?
questions.a: People will remember Yahweh’s name forever, because he defends his people and shows compassion to those who serve him.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about the nations’ idols?
questions.a: They are handmade statues of silver and gold that have mouths, eyes, and ears but they do not speak, see, hear, nor breathe.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about people who make or trust in idols?
questions.a: Those who make idols and those who trust in them will become as helpless as the lifeless idols are.
The descendants of Israel, Aaron, Levi, and those that revere and honor Yahweh should bless Yahweh.

commentary.text: God to be praised for his mercy.

Verses 1–4 The subject-matter of praise, is the blessings of grace flowing from the everlasting love of God. The name of God as a covenant God and Father in Christ, blessing us with all spiritual blessings in him, is to be loved and praised. The Lord chose a people to himself, that they might be unto him for a name and a praise. If they do not praise him for this distinguishing favour, they are the most unworthy and ungrateful of all people.

God is, and will be always, the same to his church, a gracious, faithful, wonder-working God. And his church is, and will be, the same to him, a thankful, praising people: thus his name endures for ever. He will return in ways of mercy to them, and will delight to do them good.

These verses arm believers against idolatry and all false worship, by showing what sort of gods the heathen worshipped. And the more deplorable the condition of the Gentile nations that worship idols, the more are we to be thankful that we know better. Let us pity, and pray for, and seek to benefit benighted heathens and deluded sinners. Let us endeavour to glorify his name, and recommend his truth, not only with our lips, but by holy lives, copying the example of Christ's goodness and truth.
